milestones.name: Other modules read the one sky and Sun, and one cloud optical depth dims direct sunlight once

items.statement: Each frame every scene contribution is lent one environment identity: source epoch and simulation time, and the true Sun (geometric direction, raw perpendicular illuminance, colour, angular radius, no attenuation applied) kept apart from the apparent surface light. The epoch changes when the sky model, the air profile or a LUT generation (a replacement of resources or model) changes, and never when only time advances and chart contents are recomputed.
items.ask: Do tests in ./dev check cover an epoch change on profile change and on device replacement, no change across a time scrub, and the true Sun staying continuous through sunset while the apparent surface light fades? Is the identity produced in one place and only read elsewhere?

items.statement: Through the lent bind-group layout and WGSL library alone, a contribution's own pipeline evaluates the five lent operations on Metal: Sun light at a world position, sky radiance along a direction, incident diffuse, aerial (T,S) from the camera to a point, and environment reflection with its split-sum pair. Each meets its handoff row H1-H5 in the design's numerical acceptance table, and the wrong lookups that H2 and H4 name fail.
items.ask: Read the referee tests. Does the contribution use only the lent layout and library, with no private chart, mip or storage-gain knowledge? Does each of H1-H5 assert the bound its row names against the reference its row names, and never against the forward pass's own output? For H2 and H4, is the expected value an f64 filtered decode written apart from the library's code, on the live product and on the known field, and does the test fail if a single-texel or single-slice lookup passes? Is their allowance the design's C/32 + 1e-5 M + Q, with Q one stored half-float step and nothing wider, on a known field whose neighbouring texels differ by at least 32 stored steps? Is one case of each row repeated at a non-unit exposure scale? Does H5 vary direction, roughness, the raw Sun's illuminance, the night term and a rewritten sky? Are the preserved referees P1-P11 unchanged in reference, cases and bound?

items.statement: In Chrome on hardware WebGPU the same five lent operations meet the same handoff rows H1-H5, wrong lookups included, with expected values from the same references and not from Metal's GPU output.
items.ask: Read the environment case. Does it run the lent operations in a real hardware Chrome session, apply the H1-H5 bounds itself, including the filtered decode of H2 and H4, and fail on a missing or unresolved row or on a wrong lookup that passes?

items.statement: With no optical-depth provider, the composed forward and cooked-volume shader text and the route stills are byte-identical to the recorded base commit on the Mac, and no texture, binding, pass or per-frame write is added.
items.ask: Read scripts/environment_products.py. Does off-parity render the base commit and the claimed commit from one cooked store through the engine tap, compare bytes with no tolerance or mask, and include a same-build rerun control and a negative control that must fail?

items.statement: The same holds in Chrome: with no provider the route stills are byte-identical to the base commit in one browser session.

A registered provider's optical depth multiplies direct sunlight by exp(-tau), read for the receiver's own world point, exactly once on every direct-Sun receiver (terrain, synthetic instances, cooked meshes and each lit march sample of the cooked volume) and changes nothing else: sky light, emission and geometric shadow are unchanged, the factor is exactly 1 outside the field's declared support, and toggling the provider resets only the history it must.
items.ask: Do GPU tests show a uniform tau of ln 2 halving the direct term, and only the direct term, on each receiver kind including the cooked volume; a field that differs between two world points giving each receiver, and each volume march sample, its own point's factor; and tau of zero, a receiver above the plane and a read outside the region all matching no provider? Is exp(-tau) one shared cloud-factor function that the direct-Sun term and the volume's march both call, never a per-receiver patch or a darkening of final colour?

items.statement: In the V1 valley on the Mac with the diagnostic provider on, shade patches cross terrain, instances and cooked meshes together in world space at the declared drift; shaded ground stays sky-lit and is not darkened again inside geometric shadow; the boundary lines up across receiver kinds.
items.inspect: Capture the valley at noon and at low Sun with the Mac real-time engine capture, provider off then on, with a slow pan. Look at whole frames and native-size crops of: a patch edge crossing from terrain onto a cooked mesh, shaded ground beside sunlit ground, a patch passing over ground already in a ridge's shadow, and the same world point over two seconds of drift.

items.statement: The same shade reads the same way in Chrome on the valley at noon and low Sun.
items.inspect: Capture the same four views with Chrome fixed-time capture and a short real-time sequence. Compare each with the Mac capture for the placement and depth of shade and for any receiver that disagrees.

items.statement: Cost on the Mac is recorded, not gated: forward GPU time and whole-frame time on the valley, paired and order-alternated with the provider off and on, and each forward pipeline's sampled-texture count with the provider on against the adapter's limit.
items.ask: Are the paired figures recorded with build, load class and order and labelled as observations? Is every forward pipeline within the sampled-texture limit read from the capability record, with the count stated?

items.statement: In Chrome the same is recorded: whole-frame time on the valley paired with the provider off and on, and each forward pipeline's sampled-texture count with the provider on against the browser adapter's limit, with every pipeline created.

milestones.quality_bar: Cloud shade crossing a landscape as in Red Dead Redemption 2 or Horizon Forbidden West: the patch dims direct sunlight only, moves in world space, agrees on every lit surface and leaves the shaded ground sky-lit, never black. The diagnostic pattern is a stand-in, so its shape and softness are not judged here. With no cloud source the scene and its cost are exactly what they were.

milestones.name: The valley's sky and sunlight pass the route in motion on Mac and Chrome, and G3s closes

items.statement: On the Mac, on the six-stop route and a continuous dawn-to-night scrub with slow pans, a clean-context reviewer finds none of: a horizontal brightness step across the ground, a flat near ridge with a hard bright rim at low Sun, a ridge lit warm with the Sun behind it, missing object shadows at sunrise, shadow acne at low Sun, a hard horizon line, or banding in the sky gradient and twilight.
items.inspect: Capture the route stops as fixed-time stills and the scrub and pans, including the Ground E pan, with the Mac real-time engine capture, TAAU on. Judge each named defect at every stop in whole frames and native-size crops, and in motion at 1x. Leave out only the moving shadow edge on the authored spur between 17.40 and 17.80 h. The held 17.4 h stop is judged, and the Ground E terrain lip is judged as a brightness step.

items.statement: The same review passes in Chrome on the same route and scrub.
items.inspect: Capture the same stops and scrub with Chrome fixed-time and real-time capture, TAAU on. Judge the same list, and note any stop where Chrome and the Mac differ in more than texture profile.

items.statement: On Metal, on the final build, the preserved referees P1-P11 and the handoff rows H1-H5 of the design's numerical acceptance table pass against the production producers with no reference, case or bound changed since M5, and the all-orders solar grid still reports all 198 rows.
items.ask: Did any reference, case, bound or test in the numerical acceptance table change in this milestone? If one did, is the change justified by the model and not by the image? Does any referee run a test-only variant of a producer instead of the production one?

items.statement: In Chrome on hardware WebGPU, on the final build, the handoff rows H1-H5 pass at their declared bounds.

Whole-frame and atmosphere pass costs on the route are recorded on the final build and, in the same session and configuration, on the commit this milestone started from; the M1 and M2 records are quoted as history only. Any visible hitch during the scrub is investigated and explained.
items.ask: Is the comparison a fresh rerun of the starting commit at a matched extent, TAAU setting, load class and alternated order, with no budget claim and no earlier record called paired? Does the evidence name the cause of each hitch seen in the scrub, or state that none was seen?

items.statement: The maturity ledger's G3s rows state implementation, correctness, visuals and device separately, and name what is not qualified: the west-lookout crossing, the exact disk match, solar sky and solar aerial accuracy against an all-orders reference, Moon, weather, calibrated night colour and physical display cadence.
items.ask: Do the ledger rows and the build plan's G3s line match the evidence, with the known defects listed and nothing claimed for a physical iPhone?

milestones.quality_bar: Time of day as in Red Dead Redemption 2 or Horizon Forbidden West: colour that moves continuously through dawn, noon, sunset, twilight and night, shadows that sit on the ground without acne or steps, and a horizon that reads as distance. Judged in words from the running game with reconstruction on, never against a target image. The parked west-lookout crossing and the deferred exact disk match are known and not judged.

milestones.name: Haze thickens from crisp air to murk under a control, and shafts of sunlight stand in it below ridges and broken cloud, on the Mac and in Chrome

items.statement: A scene that declares no view volume is untouched: its composed shader text, passes, resources and submitted frames are what they were before this milestone, on the Mac and in Chrome.
items.ask: Is the base the commit this milestone started from, recorded before any change, and does the Chrome arm run the same comparison?

items.statement: The air's aerosol amount is an input of the air profile. At its default every chart holds the bytes it held before. At two other amounts the lent Sun light and the transmittance chart meet P1's and P2's bounds against the f64 quadrature evaluated at that amount, the charts follow a change within the lag the profile declares, and a change of amount does not move the environment epoch.
items.ask: Did any existing reference, case, bound or test in the numerical acceptance table change? None may. Is the reference the existing f64 quadrature with its aerosol set, and not the shader's own integrator?

items.statement: With the view volume and clear air, the lent aerial transport to a point, read from the settled volume, matches an f64 integration of the air along that ray within the bound this milestone measures first, at P10's Sun elevations and at points from 5 m to beyond 32 km. Its night part still meets P5.
items.ask: Is the reference an f64 integration written apart from the shader? Is the bound measured on the settled volume and then asserted, and is it set beside what the 32³ product measures against the same reference?

items.statement: Inside the view volume the air's solar in-scatter is shadowed once. Behind an occluder that the shadow cascades hold, a cell takes no single-scattered sunlight; under a registered Sun-path optical depth a cell takes the cloud factor at its own position; and a registered haze scale is not applied as well. Transmittance and the night term are unchanged by either.
items.ask: Does the test show that the forward decoder's own split of solar in-scatter by a surface's shadow is not applied on top of the volume's, by comparing a shadowed surface's aerial term with the volume's value at its depth?

items.statement: The volume's history follows the frame contract: it advances only with submitted frames, a cut, a new epoch and a replaced device reset it, and after a reset the lent transport is whole in that frame and settled within the number of frames the profile declares. No pipeline or resource is created while the game runs.

As the haze control goes from a 300 km visual range to 5 km, at noon and at a 10° Sun, the land fades with distance into the sky's colour at the horizon. The sky and the farthest land meet without a line, and there is no banding, slice step or tile pattern in the haze.
items.inspect: Capture `fixed` stills with T2 engine capture at visual ranges of 300, 60, 20 and 5 km, at noon and at a 10° Sun, from 2 m and from 40 m. Judge each whole, the set side by side, and native-size crops along the horizon and across the middle distance.

items.statement: In haze of a 20 km visual range at a 10° Sun, shafts of sunlight stand below a ridge line and below the test cloud field's gaps, lined up with the sunlit and shaded ground beneath them, soft-edged, with no stair-step along their depth.
items.inspect: Capture `fixed` stills toward and across the Sun with the labelled test cloud field on and off. Judge each whole and in native-size crops of a shaft against dark terrain and of where it meets the ground.

items.statement: In a pan, a 40 m walk and a time scrub through sunset, the haze and its shafts do not crawl, flicker or trail, and after a cut they are whole in the first frame.
items.inspect: Capture `realtime` sequences of each at a 20 km visual range. Judge consecutive frames at 1x, whole and in native-size crops of a shaft's edge.

items.statement: In Chrome the haze sweep and the shafts pass M7.6's, M7.7's and M7.8's lists.
items.inspect: Capture the same stills and the pan in Chrome. Judge them by those lists, then compare native-size crops with the Mac's.

items.statement: The view volume's cost is on record: on the Mac and in Chrome, a paired record of the valley with the view volume and without gives the whole frame, each added pass's GPU time by name, the grid chosen and the bytes of each resource. A visible hitch, a pass about 25% over its last comparable record, or a cost that grows faster than the grid has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.
items.ask: Is the record paired, with load and order, on this milestone's work, and is the Chrome record beside it? Does it say which grid sizes were tried and what the look lost or kept at each?

items.statement: The maturity ledger's atmosphere rows state implementation, correctness, visuals and device apart for the view volume and the haze input, and name what is not qualified: the joint volume against an all-orders reference, and local lights in the air.
items.ask: Do the rows claim only what this milestone proved, on the targets it ran on?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained image.

milestones.quality_bar: Haze and light shafts as in Red Dead Redemption 2: distance that fades into the sky's own colour over a range the weather sets, and sunlight that stands in the air as soft shafts lined up with the shadows on the ground, steady as the camera moves.

milestones.name: A test bank of fog stands in the valley: the land fades into it, sunlight dims inside it, and the camera walks in and out of it, on the Mac and in Chrome

items.statement: The view volume integrates a provider's medium coefficients jointly with the air. For a uniform slab of known extinction, solar kernel and ambient source standing in the air, the lent aerial transport to points before, inside and beyond the slab matches the retained joint reference within the bound this milestone measures first, with the grid's slices as they are and with twice as many. The coefficients are summed with the air's before integration: composing the slab's own pair with the air's pair gives a different answer on a case the test names, and that answer fails.
items.ask: Is the joint reference `scripts/reference/atmosphere/joint_reference.py` or an f64 evaluation written apart from the shader? Does the wrong composition fail by more than the bound?

items.statement: A ray that leaves the volume composes once. Sky radiance, the Sun's disc and a star seen through a slab near the camera equal the reference: the slab's transmittance times the clear-air value plus the in-scatter the slab adds. With a provider registered and its coefficients zero, sky pixels hold the same bytes as with none.
items.ask: Does the far aerial operation beyond 32 km, if `CLOUDS` has built it, compose the same terminal pair, and does the test say whether it was present?

items.statement: The Sun-path optical depth has a ground band. With one registered, the factor on terrain, synthetic instances, cooked meshes, each lit sample of the cooked volume and the incident-light meter is the exponential of minus the sum of the cloud band's and the ground band's optical depth at that receiver's own position, applied once. With none registered the shaders are composed without the read, as before.
items.ask: Does the test use a ground band that differs between two heights over one point, so a read at the wrong height fails?

items.statement: A provider's near weight bounds what the volume holds: beyond the end of the ramp the volume integrates air and haze alone, and the lent transport to a point beyond it is the joint value at the ramp's end composed with clear air from there.

With the labelled test bank in the valley at noon and at a 10° Sun: the land, props and movers fade into the fog with depth along clean edges; a prop's shadow inside the fog weakens with the fog over it; the Sun's disc dims through it; toward the low Sun the fog is bright and away from it grey. There is no tile, slice or banding pattern on the fog or where it meets terrain.
items.inspect: Capture `fixed` stills with T2 engine capture at 2560×1440 from outside the bank, at its edge and inside it, toward and away from the Sun. Judge each whole and in native-size crops of the fog against a ridge, a prop and the ground.

items.statement: As the camera walks into the bank, pans inside it and walks out, and as a mover passes through its edge, nothing pops at the edge, no trail follows the mover and the exposure does not pump.
items.inspect: Capture `realtime` sequences of the walk, the pan and the mover. Judge consecutive frames at 1x, whole and in native-size crops.

items.statement: In Chrome the test bank passes M8.5's and M8.6's lists.
items.inspect: Capture the same stills and the walk in Chrome. Judge them by those lists, then compare native-size crops with the Mac's.

items.statement: The number of sampled textures each forward pipeline and the view volume's passes bind, with a ground band and a medium provider registered, is on record against the capability record and WebGPU's default limits, and every count is within its limit.
items.ask: Does `docs/evidence/ATMOSPHERE/M8-bindings.md` give the count for each pipeline and the limit it was checked against?

items.statement: With the test bank, the paired cost record is taken again on the Mac and in Chrome beside M7's, with the medium's passes timed by name. Each tripped wire has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.
items.ask: Is the record paired, with load and order, on this milestone's work, with the Chrome record beside it?

items.statement: The maturity ledger's atmosphere rows are current, with the test medium named as a stand-in that `CLOUDS` replaces.
items.ask: Do the rows claim only what this milestone proved, on the targets it ran on?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained image.

milestones.quality_bar: Fog near the camera as in Red Dead Redemption 2 and The Last of Us Part II: the land, props and movers fade into it by depth with clean edges, the Sun and its shadows weaken inside it, and nothing trails or pops as the camera passes through.
